description: We are a team of passionate developers and tech enthusiasts from Germany, focused on building innovative solutions to real-world challenges. Our strengths include software engineering, AI, cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, and full-stack development.
summary:
MARS Pathfinder is an interactive mission-planning platform that helps future Mars explorers navigate challenging terrain using real planetary data.

Built for NASA Space Apps Challenge, our project transforms Martian elevation models and scientific datasets into an interactive map where users can select destinations, compare routes optimized for distance, energy consumption, and terrain hazards, and explore potential science stops along the way.

The platform combines terrain-aware pathfinding with estimates of walking time, metabolic energy, and mission resources. Its 2D and 3D visualizations make complex planetary data easier to understand, while clearly distinguishing modeled estimates from verified measurements.

Our goal is to make Mars exploration planning more accessible, transparent, and scientifically grounded. By connecting real mission data with interactive route analysis, MARS Pathfinder demonstrates how future exploration teams could better understand trade-offs between efficiency, terrain constraints, and scientific value.
details:
The Challenge

Planning a human traverse on Mars involves more than finding the shortest path between two points. Astronauts must consider steep terrain, limited energy and oxygen, travel time, and the scientific value of potential destinations. Planetary datasets contain valuable information for these decisions, but they are often difficult to explore together in an accessible, interactive environment.

Our Solution

MARS Pathfinder combines real Martian terrain and mission data into an interactive exploration and route-planning platform focused on Jezero Crater, the landing region of NASA's Perseverance rover.

Users can explore the Martian surface, select starting points and destinations, and compare routes optimized for three different objectives:

  • Shortest distance: Minimize total travel distance.
  • Lowest energy: Minimize estimated walking energy expenditure.
  • Lowest terrain hazard: Minimize a project-defined slope-hazard exposure measure.

Users can also incorporate scientific destinations based on real Perseverance sample locations and other planetary features, allowing them to examine how science objectives change the route.

Explore the Project

MARS Pathfinder offers two complementary interactive experiences, each highlighting a different aspect of Martian exploration and mission planning.

3D Mars Explorer — Original Experience

https://nasa.lennardwlg.de/

Explore Mars through our original 3D interface, featuring planetary visualization, immersive terrain exploration, and mission-planning tools. This experience also includes an extended guided jury tour.

Advanced Terrain Map — Scientific Planning Interface

https://nasa.lennardwlg.de/karte

Access our redesigned, advanced map with detailed terrain visualization, interactive route planning, scientific locations, elevation data, and comparisons of distance, energy consumption, and terrain hazards.

30-Second Guided Demo — Recommended Starting Point

https://nasa.lennardwlg.de/karte?demo=1

Short on time? Start here! Our automated 30-second walkthrough introduces the advanced map, demonstrates terrain analysis, and highlights how different route-planning objectives affect mission decisions.

Both interfaces are part of the same MARS Pathfinder platform. The original experience emphasizes immersive planetary exploration, while the advanced map focuses on detailed scientific analysis and route optimization.

How It Works

The backend processes digital elevation models and geospatial datasets from NASA and USGS sources. Terrain is represented as a grid-based graph, and a shortest-path algorithm calculates routes using different cost functions.

The system estimates route distance, walking duration, metabolic energy expenditure, and oxygen requirements. Interactive maps, elevation profiles, and 3D terrain views help users understand the relationship between topography, route selection, and mission resources.

Technology

We developed the platform using TypeScript, React, Next.js, Three.js, and Python. The backend uses FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, and Rasterio for geospatial processing, scientific calculations, and route optimization. The redesigned map also uses Leaflet.

Creativity and Impact

MARS Pathfinder connects authentic planetary datasets, computational route optimization, and interactive visualization in a single exploration experience.

Rather than presenting one supposedly optimal route, the platform makes competing mission objectives visible and comparable. This helps students, researchers, and space enthusiasts understand why exploration planning requires trade-offs between distance, energy, terrain constraints, and scientific opportunity.

Scientific Transparency

MARS Pathfinder is a research and educational prototype, not an operational astronaut navigation system. Terrain resolution limits the detection of small obstacles, physiological estimates depend on simplifying assumptions, and our terrain-hazard index is not a measured accident probability.

We document data provenance, modeling assumptions, and known limitations so users can distinguish measured planetary data from computational estimates.
